Director or Scheduling Representative if you have any questions.

HOURLY TAKES ADVISORY – MARKET DELIVERY ZONE

HOURLY TAKES ADVISORY – MARKET
DELIVERY ZONE 

 

Due to the impending colder
weather and current system operating conditions, effective for
 Friday, December
 12, 2025, at 9:00 am., and continuing until further notice
, per Natural's
tariff [GT&C Section 7.4], 
Shippers and Point Operators
 are advised
to 
limit hourly
 
takes
 at 
ALL DELIVERY POINTS IN THE MARKET
DELIVERY ZONE
.  Additionally, Natural continues to monitor operating
conditions system wide.  If necessary, Natural will issue Operational Flow
Orders (OFOs) to address Shipper actions that are 
detrimental to such
operating conditions outside the Market Delivery Zone
.  Should Natural's
ability to provide hourly flexibility decrease, an Operational Flow Order (OFO)
condition will occur.

 

As provided in the tariff,
at each point in the Market Delivery Zone, the hourly rights for each Shipper/Point
Operator will be limited.  Such hourly rights will be limited by service
priority and nomination cycle, based on hours remaining in the gas day. 
Shippers and Point Operators are responsible for calculating and monitoring
their hourly usage so as not to exceed the limits described herein.

 

Hourly Rights for Firm
Service – 150%

Includes Primary and
Secondary Confirmed Nominations and Unused No-Notice firm service rights

 

            
Timely/Evening
Cycles

Limited to 
6.25% (150% / 24 hours)
 of Firm
Service.  

 

Intra-Day 1 Cycle

Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous
cycle for Firm Service; plus 
7.895%
 
(150% / 19 hours)
 of the difference
of current cycle Firm Service minus prior cycle Firm Service.  

 

Intra-Day 2 Cycle

Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous
cycle for Firm Service; plus
 10.00% (150% / 15 hours)
 of the difference
of current cycle Firm Service minus prior cycle Firm Service.  

 

Intra-Day 3 Cycle

Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous
cycle for Firm Service, plus 
13.64% (150% / 11 hours)
 of the difference
of current cycle Firm Service minus prior cycle Firm Service.

 

 

Hourly Rights for
Interruptible Service – 105%

Includes Interruptible and
AOR nominations, as well as POA tolerances

 

Timely/Evening
Cycles

Limited to 
4.375% (105% / 24 hours)
 of Interruptible
Service.  

 

Intra-Day 1 Cycle

Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous
cycle for Interruptible Service; plus
 5.53%
 
(105% / 19 hours)
 of
the difference of current cycle Interruptible Service minus prior cycle Interruptible
Service.  

 

 

Intra-Day 2 Cycle

Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous
cycle for Interruptible Service; plus 
7.0% (105% / 15 hours)
 of the
difference of current cycle Interruptible Service minus prior cycle Interruptible
Service.  

 

Intra-Day 3 Cycle

Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous
cycle for Interruptible Service; plus 
9.55% (105% / 11 hours)
 of the
difference of current cycle Interruptible Service minus prior cycle
Interruptible Service.

 

Limitation on
Nominations in All Cycles for Firm and Interruptible Service

 

Shippers are advised that nominations should be
received by Timely/Evening Cycle in order to utilize full rights over 24 hours,
to avoid exceeding the 24 hour ratable hourly takes calculation.  In all
cases, any first time nominations received on Non-Timely Cycles for full MDQ
utilization rights, plus any scheduled ITS nominations must conform to the 24
hour ratable calculation.  Shipper's hourly rights based on firm MDQ, plus
interruptible nominations, must be adequate enough to accommodate the
calculated hourly rights for the remaining hours of the gas day. 
Specifically, hourly rights cannot exceed 150% / 24 hours of Shipper's MDQ on
the nominated contract, plus 105% / 24 hours of Shipper's interruptible
nominations.

 

In addition, Natural would
like to remind point operators to utilize the Operator Point Reports available
on our website to assist you in monitoring your hourly takes.  These reports
are available by linking to http://pipeline.kindermorgan.com.  Select NGPL >
Customer Activities > Log On > Flowing Gas > Additional Reports >
NGPL/HRZ > NGPL/HRZ – Hourly Nomination Details.

 

Please contact your Account
Director or Scheduling Representative if you have any questions.

ANR/NGPL SOUTH JOLIET AT CAPACITY

SEGMENT
25 – STATION MAINTENANCE – CS 302

 

As
posted on Natural's Outage Impact Report (X25-1527903), Natural will be
performing station maintenance at Compressor Station 302 (CS 302) located in Montgomery
County, Texas (Segment 25 of Natural's Texok Zone).  Natural is required to
reduce the maximum operating capacity eastbound into Segment 25 from Segment 26
and Segment 22, thus limiting Natural's throughput capacity eastbound through
CS 302 during this restriction.

 

The

scheduling constraint will be at CS 302
; therefore, any gas received
west of CS 302 for delivery east of CS 302 will be impacted for the duration of
the restriction.  The Pooling Point - Texok Zone (LOC 10560) is located west of
the constraint.  Firm transportation associated with storage withdrawals may be
impacted.

 

As
such, effective for gas day 
Wednesday, April 1, 2026, Timely Cycle, and
continuing through gas day Friday, May 1, 2026
, Natural will schedule
Primary Firm and Secondary in-path Firm transports to no less than 
55%

of contract MDQ through CS 302.  AOR/ITS and Secondary out-of-path Firm
transports 
will not
 be available for the duration of this restriction.

 

The
stated scheduling percentage is based upon the current level of firm capacity
contracted for during this restriction and is subject to change based upon
operational conditions and Shipper utilization.

 

Continue
to monitor Natural's interactive website for any updates.  Please contact your
Account Director or Scheduling Representative if you have any questions.

HOURLY TAKES ADVISORY – MARKET DELIVERY ZONE HOURLY TAKES ADVISORY – MARKET DELIVERY ZONE Due to the impending colder weather and current system operating conditions, effective for Friday, December 12, 2025, at 9:00 am., and continuing until further notice , per Natural's tariff [GT&C Section 7.4], Shippers and Point Operators are advised to limit hourly takes at ALL DELIVERY POINTS IN THE MARKET DELIVERY ZONE . Additionally, Natural continues to monitor operating conditions system wide. If necessary, Natural will issue Operational Flow Orders (OFOs) to address Shipper actions that are detrimental to such operating conditions outside the Market Delivery Zone . Should Natural's ability to provide hourly flexibility decrease, an Operational Flow Order (OFO) condition will occur. As provided in the tariff, at each point in the Market Delivery Zone, the hourly rights for each Shipper/Point Operator will be limited. Such hourly rights will be limited by service priority and nomination cycle, based on hours remaining in the gas day. Shippers and Point Operators are responsible for calculating and monitoring their hourly usage so as not to exceed the limits described herein. Hourly Rights for Firm Service – 150% Includes Primary and Secondary Confirmed Nominations and Unused No-Notice firm service rights Timely/Evening Cycles Limited to 6.25% (150% / 24 hours) of Firm Service. Intra-Day 1 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Firm Service; plus 7.895% (150% / 19 hours) of the difference of current cycle Firm Service minus prior cycle Firm Service. Intra-Day 2 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Firm Service; plus 10.00% (150% / 15 hours) of the difference of current cycle Firm Service minus prior cycle Firm Service. Intra-Day 3 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Firm Service, plus 13.64% (150% / 11 hours) of the difference of current cycle Firm Service minus prior cycle Firm Service. Hourly Rights for Interruptible Service – 105% Includes Interruptible and AOR nominations, as well as POA tolerances Timely/Evening Cycles Limited to 4.375% (105% / 24 hours) of Interruptible Service. Intra-Day 1 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Interruptible Service; plus 5.53% (105% / 19 hours) of the difference of current cycle Interruptible Service minus prior cycle Interruptible Service. Intra-Day 2 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Interruptible Service; plus 7.0% (105% / 15 hours) of the difference of current cycle Interruptible Service minus prior cycle Interruptible Service. Intra-Day 3 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Interruptible Service; plus 9.55% (105% / 11 hours) of the difference of current cycle Interruptible Service minus prior cycle Interruptible Service. Limitation on Nominations in All Cycles for Firm and Interruptible Service Shippers are advised that nominations should be received by Timely/Evening Cycle in order to utilize full rights over 24 hours, to avoid exceeding the 24 hour ratable hourly takes calculation. In all cases, any first time nominations received on Non-Timely Cycles for full MDQ utilization rights, plus any scheduled ITS nominations must conform to the 24 hour ratable calculation. Shipper's hourly rights based on firm MDQ, plus interruptible nominations, must be adequate enough to accommodate the calculated hourly rights for the remaining hours of the gas day. Specifically, hourly rights cannot exceed 150% / 24 hours of Shipper's MDQ on the nominated contract, plus 105% / 24 hours of Shipper's interruptible nominations. In addition, Natural would like to remind point operators to utilize the Operator Point Reports available on our website to assist you in monitoring your hourly takes. These reports are available by linking to http://pipeline.kindermorgan.com. Select NGPL > Customer Activities > Log On > Flowing Gas > Additional Reports > NGPL/HRZ > NGPL/HRZ – Hourly Nomination Details. Please contact your Account Director or Scheduling Representative if you have any questions. ..

HOURLY TAKES ADVISORY – MARKET DELIVERY ZONE HOURLY TAKES ADVISORY – MARKET DELIVERY ZONE Due to the impending colder weather and current system operating conditions, effective for Friday, December 12, 2025, at 9:00 am., and continuing until further notice , per Natural's tariff [GT&C Section 7.4], Shippers and Point Operators are advised to limit hourly takes at ALL DELIVERY POINTS IN THE MARKET DELIVERY ZONE . Additionally, Natural continues to monitor operating conditions system wide. If necessary, Natural will issue Operational Flow Orders (OFOs) to address Shipper actions that are detrimental to such operating conditions outside the Market Delivery Zone . Should Natural's ability to provide hourly flexibility decrease, an Operational Flow Order (OFO) condition will occur. As provided in the tariff, at each point in the Market Delivery Zone, the hourly rights for each Shipper/Point Operator will be limited. Such hourly rights will be limited by service priority and nomination cycle, based on hours remaining in the gas day. Shippers and Point Operators are responsible for calculating and monitoring their hourly usage so as not to exceed the limits described herein. Hourly Rights for Firm Service – 150% Includes Primary and Secondary Confirmed Nominations and Unused No-Notice firm service rights Timely/Evening Cycles Limited to 6.25% (150% / 24 hours) of Firm Service. Intra-Day 1 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Firm Service; plus 7.895% (150% / 19 hours) of the difference of current cycle Firm Service minus prior cycle Firm Service. Intra-Day 2 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Firm Service; plus 10.00% (150% / 15 hours) of the difference of current cycle Firm Service minus prior cycle Firm Service. Intra-Day 3 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Firm Service, plus 13.64% (150% / 11 hours) of the difference of current cycle Firm Service minus prior cycle Firm Service. Hourly Rights for Interruptible Service – 105% Includes Interruptible and AOR nominations, as well as POA tolerances Timely/Evening Cycles Limited to 4.375% (105% / 24 hours) of Interruptible Service. Intra-Day 1 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Interruptible Service; plus 5.53% (105% / 19 hours) of the difference of current cycle Interruptible Service minus prior cycle Interruptible Service. Intra-Day 2 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Interruptible Service; plus 7.0% (105% / 15 hours) of the difference of current cycle Interruptible Service minus prior cycle Interruptible Service. Intra-Day 3 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Interruptible Service; plus 9.55% (105% / 11 hours) of the difference of current cycle Interruptible Service minus prior cycle Interruptible Service. Limitation on Nominations in All Cycles for Firm and Interruptible Service Shippers are advised that nominations should be received by Timely/Evening Cycle in order to utilize full rights over 24 hours, to avoid exceeding the 24 hour ratable hourly takes calculation. In all cases, any first time nominations received on Non-Timely Cycles for full MDQ utilization rights, plus any scheduled ITS nominations must conform to the 24 hour ratable calculation. Shipper's hourly rights based on firm MDQ, plus interruptible nominations, must be adequate enough to accommodate the calculated hourly rights for the remaining hours of the gas day. Specifically, hourly rights cannot exceed 150% / 24 hours of Shipper's MDQ on the nominated contract, plus 105% / 24 hours of Shipper's interruptible nominations. In addition, Natural would like to remind point operators to utilize the Operator Point Reports available on our website to assist you in monitoring your hourly takes. These reports are available by linking to http://pipeline.kindermorgan.com. Select NGPL > Customer Activities > Log On > Flowing Gas > Additional Reports > NGPL/HRZ > NGPL/HRZ – Hourly Nomination Details. Please contact your Account Director or Scheduling Representative if you have any questions. ..

Natural is required to reduce the maximum operating capacity eastbound into Segment 25 from Segment 26 and Segment 22, thus limiting Natural's throughput capacity eastbound through CS 302 during this restriction. The scheduling constraint will be at CS 302 ; therefore, any gas received west of CS 302 for delivery east of CS 302 will be impacted for the duration of the restriction. The Pooling Point - Texok Zone (LOC 10560) is located west of the constraint. Firm transportation associated with storage withdrawals may be impacted. As such, effective for gas day Wednesday, April 1, 2026, Timely Cycle, and continuing through gas day Friday, May 1, 2026 , Natural will schedule Primary Firm and Secondary in-path Firm transports to no less than 55% of contract MDQ through CS 302. AOR/ITS and Secondary out-of-path Firm transports will not be available for the duration of this restriction. The stated scheduling percentage is based upon the current level of firm capacity contracted for during this restriction and is subject to change based upon operational conditions and Shipper utilization. Continue to monitor Natural's interactive website for any updates. Please contact your Account Director or Scheduling Representative if you have any questions. ..

OPERATIONAL
FLOW ORDER – MARKET DELIVERY ZONE – REPORT

On January 20, 2026, due
to forecasted colder than normal weather, expected increased load on its
system, anticipated maximum peaking withdrawals from storage facilities, and
system operating conditions, Natural issued an Operational Flow Order (“OFO”) in
the Market Delivery Zone effective for Thursday, January 22, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. Central
Clock Time. This action was taken in accordance with Section 23.6 of the
General Terms and Conditions of Natural's FERC Gas Tariff (“GT&C”).

The OFO was issued to
maintain and preserve the operational integrity of Natural's system and was in
response to the following operational factors: (1) to maintain pressures for
firm transportation deliveries in the Market Delivery Zone; and (2) maintain deliverability
from Natural's market area storage fields for firm storage services.

The OFO did not result in
any curtailment of primary firm service.  During the OFO, Natural implemented
daily and hourly take limitations for firm and interruptible Shippers
(including Point Operators) at all points in the Market Delivery Zone.  The OFO
limited Shippers and Point Operators, on a daily basis, from taking volumes in
excess of confirmed transportation nominations plus no-notice rights at
delivery points in the Market Delivery Zone, and on an hourly basis to 130% of
their firm service rights.  Hourly rights for interruptible nominations were
limited to 105% of the Shipper's interruptible nominations. Additionally,
Shippers and Point Operators were required to flow more ratably during the gas
day based on service priority and nomination cycles.  
The
firm service percentage was reduced to 110% on Tuesday, January 27, 2026 at
9:00 a.m. Central Clock Time, and then  increased back to 130% on Thursday
February 5, 2026 at 9:00 am Central Clock Time. 
 

These measures were taken
consistent with Natural's Tariff due to sustained colder than normal weather in
the Market Delivery Zone and anticipated maximum peaking withdrawals from
storage facilities.  As the weather conditions moderated and the associated
high gas demand declined, Natural removed the OFO, effective at 9:00 a.m. on
gas day Monday, February 9, 2026.

This posting complies
with GT&C Section 23.6(h) of Natural's Tariff to describe the specific
operational factors which caused the Operational Flow Order to be issued and to
be lifted.

HOURLY TAKES ADVISORY – MARKET DELIVERY ZONE HOURLY TAKES ADVISORY – MARKET DELIVERY ZONE Due to the impending colder weather and current system operating conditions, effective for Friday, December 12, 2025, at 9:00 am., and continuing until further notice , per Natural's tariff [GT&C Section 7.4], Shippers and Point Operators are advised to limit hourly takes at ALL DELIVERY POINTS IN THE MARKET DELIVERY ZONE . Additionally, Natural continues to monitor operating conditions system wide. If necessary, Natural will issue Operational Flow Orders (OFOs) to address Shipper actions that are detrimental to such operating conditions outside the Market Delivery Zone . Should Natural's ability to provide hourly flexibility decrease, an Operational Flow Order (OFO) condition will occur. As provided in the tariff, at each point in the Market Delivery Zone, the hourly rights for each Shipper/Point Operator will be limited. Such hourly rights will be limited by service priority and nomination cycle, based on hours remaining in the gas day. Shippers and Point Operators are responsible for calculating and monitoring their hourly usage so as not to exceed the limits described herein. Hourly Rights for Firm Service – 150% Includes Primary and Secondary Confirmed Nominations and Unused No-Notice firm service rights Timely/Evening Cycles Limited to 6.25% (150% / 24 hours) of Firm Service. Intra-Day 1 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Firm Service; plus 7.895% (150% / 19 hours) of the difference of current cycle Firm Service minus prior cycle Firm Service. Intra-Day 2 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Firm Service; plus 10.00% (150% / 15 hours) of the difference of current cycle Firm Service minus prior cycle Firm Service. Intra-Day 3 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Firm Service, plus 13.64% (150% / 11 hours) of the difference of current cycle Firm Service minus prior cycle Firm Service. Hourly Rights for Interruptible Service – 105% Includes Interruptible and AOR nominations, as well as POA tolerances Timely/Evening Cycles Limited to 4.375% (105% / 24 hours) of Interruptible Service. Intra-Day 1 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Interruptible Service; plus 5.53% (105% / 19 hours) of the difference of current cycle Interruptible Service minus prior cycle Interruptible Service. Intra-Day 2 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Interruptible Service; plus 7.0% (105% / 15 hours) of the difference of current cycle Interruptible Service minus prior cycle Interruptible Service. Intra-Day 3 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Interruptible Service; plus 9.55% (105% / 11 hours) of the difference of current cycle Interruptible Service minus prior cycle Interruptible Service. Limitation on Nominations in All Cycles for Firm and Interruptible Service Shippers are advised that nominations should be received by Timely/Evening Cycle in order to utilize full rights over 24 hours, to avoid exceeding the 24 hour ratable hourly takes calculation. In all cases, any first time nominations received on Non-Timely Cycles for full MDQ utilization rights, plus any scheduled ITS nominations must conform to the 24 hour ratable calculation. Shipper's hourly rights based on firm MDQ, plus interruptible nominations, must be adequate enough to accommodate the calculated hourly rights for the remaining hours of the gas day. Specifically, hourly rights cannot exceed 150% / 24 hours of Shipper's MDQ on the nominated contract, plus 105% / 24 hours of Shipper's interruptible nominations. In addition, Natural would like to remind point operators to utilize the Operator Point Reports available on our website to assist you in monitoring your hourly takes. These reports are available by linking to http://pipeline.kindermorgan.com. Select NGPL > Customer Activities > Log On > Flowing Gas > Additional Reports > NGPL/HRZ > NGPL/HRZ – Hourly Nomination Details. Please contact your Account Director or Scheduling Representative if you have any questions. ..

STATION 302 – REPLACE REGULATOR – UPDATE

PHMSA MEGA RULE–- ELIGIBLE
PROJECT
 - SEGMENT 13 – AMARILLO #3 M/L – CS 107/108 – ILI TOOL
RUNS

 

In accordance with its FERC
Gas Tariff and as posted on Natural's Outage Impact Report 
(X25-1166550)
; 
as part of
Natural's ongoing pipeline Integrity Management Program, Natural will perform a
series of ILI tool runs on its Amarillo #3 mainline between Compressor Station 107
(CS 107) located in Mills County, Iowa and Compressor Station 108 (CS 108)
located in Warren County, Iowa (Segment 13 of Natural's Amarillo Mainline Zone). 
The tool runs will require Natural to reduce the operating capacity, thus limiting
Natural's throughput capacity northbound through CS 108.  Once the data
from the tool runs have been analyzed, any remediation work impacting shippers
will be posted.

 

This remediation project is
pursuant to the PHMSA Mega Rule and as set forth in its Tariff, is an Eligible
Project (ID 4819) included on the Eligible Project List posted on Natural's
internet website.  See Eligible Project ID, line name and location
identified below (Appendix F- Docket No. RP22-1222 Settlement).  This
outage is subject to the provisions of Section 5.2 (c) (5) of the General
Terms and Conditions of Natural's FERC Gas Tariff.

 

Project
ID          Line
Name                  
              Location/Segment
No.                      
           

4819                  AMARILLO
#3 MAINLINE     SEGMENT 13

 

The scheduling
constraint will be upstream of CS 108 at the beginning of Segment 13;
therefore, any gas received south of Segment 13 for delivery north of Segment
13 will be impacted for the duration of the restriction.  Receipts from
Trailblazer Gage (LOC 902900) are south of CS 107 and will be impacted for the
duration of the restriction.  Northern Natural Mills (LOC 900203) is located
downstream of the Segment 13 constraint location.  For scheduling purposes, the
Amarillo Pool (LOC 10566) is located south of the constraint. 
Additionally, firm transportation associated with storage withdrawals or
injections may be impacted.

 

As such,
effective on the gas days indicated below, Natural will schedule Primary Firm and
Secondary in-path Firm transports to no less than 
44%
 of contract
MDQ northbound through CS 107.  AOR/ITS and Secondary out-of-path Firm
transports 
will not
 be available for the duration of the restriction.

 

TOOL RUN
DATES
:

 

Gas day Friday,
April 17, 2026 (Cleaning/ Gauge Tools)

Gas day
Tuesday, April 21, 2026 (Cleaning Tool)

Gas day Thursday,
April 23, 2026 (Cleaning Tool)

Gas day Tuesday,
April 28, 2026 (Combo Tool)

Gas day Thursday,
April 30, 2026 (EMAT Tool)

Gas day
Friday, May 1, 2026 (EMAT Tool)

 

The stated
scheduling percentage is based upon the current level of firm capacity
contracted for during this restriction and is subject to change based upon
operational conditions and Shipper utilization.

 

Continue to
monitor Natural's interactive website for any updates to the end date and/or
scheduling percentage during this restriction.  Please contact your
Account Director or Scheduling Representative if you have any questions.

OPERATIONAL FLOW ORDER – MARKET DELIVERY ZONE – REPORT On January 20, 2026, due to forecasted colder than normal weather, expected increased load on its system, anticipated maximum peaking withdrawals from storage facilities, and system operating conditions, Natural issued an Operational Flow Order (“OFO”) in the Market Delivery Zone effective for Thursday, January 22, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. Central Clock Time. This action was taken in accordance with Section 23.6 of the General Terms and Conditions of Natural's FERC Gas Tariff (“GT&C”). The OFO was issued to maintain and preserve the operational integrity of Natural's system and was in response to the following operational factors: (1) to maintain pressures for firm transportation deliveries in the Market Delivery Zone; and (2) maintain deliverability from Natural's market area storage fields for firm storage services. The OFO did not result in any curtailment of primary firm service. During the OFO, Natural implemented daily and hourly take limitations for firm and interruptible Shippers (including Point Operators) at all points in the Market Delivery Zone. The OFO limited Shippers and Point Operators, on a daily basis, from taking volumes in excess of confirmed transportation nominations plus no-notice rights at delivery points in the Market Delivery Zone, and on an hourly basis to 130% of their firm service rights. Hourly rights for interruptible nominations were limited to 105% of the Shipper's interruptible nominations. Additionally, Shippers and Point Operators were required to flow more ratably during the gas day based on service priority and nomination cycles. The firm service percentage was reduced to 110% on Tuesday, January 27, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. Central Clock Time, and then increased back to 130% on Thursday February 5, 2026 at 9:00 am Central Clock Time. These measures were taken consistent with Natural's Tariff due to sustained colder than normal weather in the Market Delivery Zone and anticipated maximum peaking withdrawals from storage facilities. As the weather conditions moderated and the associated high gas demand declined, Natural removed the OFO, effective at 9:00 a.m. on gas day Monday, February 9, 2026. This posting complies with GT&C Section 23.6(h) of Natural's Tariff to describe the specific operational factors which caused the Operational Flow Order to be issued and to be lifted. ..

northbound into Segment 8 from Segment 9, thus limiting Natural's throughput

The scheduling constraint

restriction.  The Pooling Point - Permian Zone (LOC 25077) is located
south of the constraint.  Firm transportation associated with storage
withdrawals may be impacted.

 

As such, effective for gas
day 
Tuesday, April 7, 2026, Timely
Cycle and continuing until further notice
, Natural will schedule Primary Firm and Secondary in-path Firm
transports to no less than 
94%
 of contract MDQ through CS 167.  AOR/ITS and
Secondary out-of-path Firm transports 
will not
 be available for the
duration of this restriction.

 

Additionally, the unit
maintenance referenced on Natural's Outage Impact Report (X26-220667) has been
postponed until further notice
.

 

The stated scheduling
percentage is based upon the current level of firm capacity contracted for
during this restriction and is subject to change based upon operational
conditions and Shipper utilization.

 

Continue to monitor Natural's
interactive website for any updates to the end date during this
restriction.  Please contact your Account Director or Scheduling
Representative if you have any questions.

HOURLY TAKES ADVISORY – MARKET DELIVERY ZONE HOURLY TAKES ADVISORY – MARKET DELIVERY ZONE Due to the impending colder weather and current system operating conditions, effective for Friday, December 12, 2025, at 9:00 am., and continuing until further notice , per Natural's tariff [GT&C Section 7.4], Shippers and Point Operators are advised to limit hourly takes at ALL DELIVERY POINTS IN THE MARKET DELIVERY ZONE . Additionally, Natural continues to monitor operating conditions system wide. If necessary, Natural will issue Operational Flow Orders (OFOs) to address Shipper actions that are detrimental to such operating conditions outside the Market Delivery Zone . Should Natural's ability to provide hourly flexibility decrease, an Operational Flow Order (OFO) condition will occur. As provided in the tariff, at each point in the Market Delivery Zone, the hourly rights for each Shipper/Point Operator will be limited. Such hourly rights will be limited by service priority and nomination cycle, based on hours remaining in the gas day. Shippers and Point Operators are responsible for calculating and monitoring their hourly usage so as not to exceed the limits described herein. Hourly Rights for Firm Service – 150% Includes Primary and Secondary Confirmed Nominations and Unused No-Notice firm service rights Timely/Evening Cycles Limited to 6.25% (150% / 24 hours) of Firm Service. Intra-Day 1 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Firm Service; plus 7.895% (150% / 19 hours) of the difference of current cycle Firm Service minus prior cycle Firm Service. Intra-Day 2 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Firm Service; plus 10.00% (150% / 15 hours) of the difference of current cycle Firm Service minus prior cycle Firm Service. Intra-Day 3 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Firm Service, plus 13.64% (150% / 11 hours) of the difference of current cycle Firm Service minus prior cycle Firm Service. Hourly Rights for Interruptible Service – 105% Includes Interruptible and AOR nominations, as well as POA tolerances Timely/Evening Cycles Limited to 4.375% (105% / 24 hours) of Interruptible Service. Intra-Day 1 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Interruptible Service; plus 5.53% (105% / 19 hours) of the difference of current cycle Interruptible Service minus prior cycle Interruptible Service. Intra-Day 2 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Interruptible Service; plus 7.0% (105% / 15 hours) of the difference of current cycle Interruptible Service minus prior cycle Interruptible Service. Intra-Day 3 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Interruptible Service; plus 9.55% (105% / 11 hours) of the difference of current cycle Interruptible Service minus prior cycle Interruptible Service. Limitation on Nominations in All Cycles for Firm and Interruptible Service Shippers are advised that nominations should be received by Timely/Evening Cycle in order to utilize full rights over 24 hours, to avoid exceeding the 24 hour ratable hourly takes calculation. In all cases, any first time nominations received on Non-Timely Cycles for full MDQ utilization rights, plus any scheduled ITS nominations must conform to the 24 hour ratable calculation. Shipper's hourly rights based on firm MDQ, plus interruptible nominations, must be adequate enough to accommodate the calculated hourly rights for the remaining hours of the gas day. Specifically, hourly rights cannot exceed 150% / 24 hours of Shipper's MDQ on the nominated contract, plus 105% / 24 hours of Shipper's interruptible nominations. In addition, Natural would like to remind point operators to utilize the Operator Point Reports available on our website to assist you in monitoring your hourly takes. These reports are available by linking to http://pipeline.kindermorgan.com. Select NGPL > Customer Activities > Log On > Flowing Gas > Additional Reports > NGPL/HRZ > NGPL/HRZ – Hourly Nomination Details. Please contact your Account Director or Scheduling Representative if you have any questions. ..

OPERATIONAL FLOW ORDER – MARKET DELIVERY ZONE – REPORT On January 20, 2026, due to forecasted colder than normal weather, expected increased load on its system, anticipated maximum peaking withdrawals from storage facilities, and system operating conditions, Natural issued an Operational Flow Order (“OFO”) in the Market Delivery Zone effective for Thursday, January 22, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. Central Clock Time. This action was taken in accordance with Section 23.6 of the General Terms and Conditions of Natural's FERC Gas Tariff (“GT&C”). The OFO was issued to maintain and preserve the operational integrity of Natural's system and was in response to the following operational factors: (1) to maintain pressures for firm transportation deliveries in the Market Delivery Zone; and (2) maintain deliverability from Natural's market area storage fields for firm storage services. The OFO did not result in any curtailment of primary firm service. During the OFO, Natural implemented daily and hourly take limitations for firm and interruptible Shippers (including Point Operators) at all points in the Market Delivery Zone. The OFO limited Shippers and Point Operators, on a daily basis, from taking volumes in excess of confirmed transportation nominations plus no-notice rights at delivery points in the Market Delivery Zone, and on an hourly basis to 130% of their firm service rights. Hourly rights for interruptible nominations were limited to 105% of the Shipper's interruptible nominations. Additionally, Shippers and Point Operators were required to flow more ratably during the gas day based on service priority and nomination cycles. The firm service percentage was reduced to 110% on Tuesday, January 27, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. Central Clock Time, and then increased back to 130% on Thursday February 5, 2026 at 9:00 am Central Clock Time. These measures were taken consistent with Natural's Tariff due to sustained colder than normal weather in the Market Delivery Zone and anticipated maximum peaking withdrawals from storage facilities. As the weather conditions moderated and the associated high gas demand declined, Natural removed the OFO, effective at 9:00 a.m. on gas day Monday, February 9, 2026. This posting complies with GT&C Section 23.6(h) of Natural's Tariff to describe the specific operational factors which caused the Operational Flow Order to be issued and to be lifted. ..

HOURLY TAKES ADVISORY – MARKET DELIVERY ZONE HOURLY TAKES ADVISORY – MARKET DELIVERY ZONE Due to the impending colder weather and current system operating conditions, effective for Friday, December 12, 2025, at 9:00 am., and continuing until further notice , per Natural's tariff [GT&C Section 7.4], Shippers and Point Operators are advised to limit hourly takes at ALL DELIVERY POINTS IN THE MARKET DELIVERY ZONE . Additionally, Natural continues to monitor operating conditions system wide. If necessary, Natural will issue Operational Flow Orders (OFOs) to address Shipper actions that are detrimental to such operating conditions outside the Market Delivery Zone . Should Natural's ability to provide hourly flexibility decrease, an Operational Flow Order (OFO) condition will occur. As provided in the tariff, at each point in the Market Delivery Zone, the hourly rights for each Shipper/Point Operator will be limited. Such hourly rights will be limited by service priority and nomination cycle, based on hours remaining in the gas day. Shippers and Point Operators are responsible for calculating and monitoring their hourly usage so as not to exceed the limits described herein. Hourly Rights for Firm Service – 150% Includes Primary and Secondary Confirmed Nominations and Unused No-Notice firm service rights Timely/Evening Cycles Limited to 6.25% (150% / 24 hours) of Firm Service. Intra-Day 1 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Firm Service; plus 7.895% (150% / 19 hours) of the difference of current cycle Firm Service minus prior cycle Firm Service. Intra-Day 2 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Firm Service; plus 10.00% (150% / 15 hours) of the difference of current cycle Firm Service minus prior cycle Firm Service. Intra-Day 3 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Firm Service, plus 13.64% (150% / 11 hours) of the difference of current cycle Firm Service minus prior cycle Firm Service. Hourly Rights for Interruptible Service – 105% Includes Interruptible and AOR nominations, as well as POA tolerances Timely/Evening Cycles Limited to 4.375% (105% / 24 hours) of Interruptible Service. Intra-Day 1 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Interruptible Service; plus 5.53% (105% / 19 hours) of the difference of current cycle Interruptible Service minus prior cycle Interruptible Service. Intra-Day 2 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Interruptible Service; plus 7.0% (105% / 15 hours) of the difference of current cycle Interruptible Service minus prior cycle Interruptible Service. Intra-Day 3 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Interruptible Service; plus 9.55% (105% / 11 hours) of the difference of current cycle Interruptible Service minus prior cycle Interruptible Service. Limitation on Nominations in All Cycles for Firm and Interruptible Service Shippers are advised that nominations should be received by Timely/Evening Cycle in order to utilize full rights over 24 hours, to avoid exceeding the 24 hour ratable hourly takes calculation. In all cases, any first time nominations received on Non-Timely Cycles for full MDQ utilization rights, plus any scheduled ITS nominations must conform to the 24 hour ratable calculation. Shipper's hourly rights based on firm MDQ, plus interruptible nominations, must be adequate enough to accommodate the calculated hourly rights for the remaining hours of the gas day. Specifically, hourly rights cannot exceed 150% / 24 hours of Shipper's MDQ on the nominated contract, plus 105% / 24 hours of Shipper's interruptible nominations. In addition, Natural would like to remind point operators to utilize the Operator Point Reports available on our website to assist you in monitoring your hourly takes. These reports are available by linking to http://pipeline.kindermorgan.com. Select NGPL > Customer Activities > Log On > Flowing Gas > Additional Reports > NGPL/HRZ > NGPL/HRZ – Hourly Nomination Details. Please contact your Account Director or Scheduling Representative if you have any questions. ..

OPERATIONAL FLOW ORDER – MARKET DELIVERY ZONE – REPORT On January 20, 2026, due to forecasted colder than normal weather, expected increased load on its system, anticipated maximum peaking withdrawals from storage facilities, and system operating conditions, Natural issued an Operational Flow Order (“OFO”) in the Market Delivery Zone effective for Thursday, January 22, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. Central Clock Time. This action was taken in accordance with Section 23.6 of the General Terms and Conditions of Natural's FERC Gas Tariff (“GT&C”). The OFO was issued to maintain and preserve the operational integrity of Natural's system and was in response to the following operational factors: (1) to maintain pressures for firm transportation deliveries in the Market Delivery Zone; and (2) maintain deliverability from Natural's market area storage fields for firm storage services. The OFO did not result in any curtailment of primary firm service. During the OFO, Natural implemented daily and hourly take limitations for firm and interruptible Shippers (including Point Operators) at all points in the Market Delivery Zone. The OFO limited Shippers and Point Operators, on a daily basis, from taking volumes in excess of confirmed transportation nominations plus no-notice rights at delivery points in the Market Delivery Zone, and on an hourly basis to 130% of their firm service rights. Hourly rights for interruptible nominations were limited to 105% of the Shipper's interruptible nominations. Additionally, Shippers and Point Operators were required to flow more ratably during the gas day based on service priority and nomination cycles. The firm service percentage was reduced to 110% on Tuesday, January 27, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. Central Clock Time, and then increased back to 130% on Thursday February 5, 2026 at 9:00 am Central Clock Time. These measures were taken consistent with Natural's Tariff due to sustained colder than normal weather in the Market Delivery Zone and anticipated maximum peaking withdrawals from storage facilities. As the weather conditions moderated and the associated high gas demand declined, Natural removed the OFO, effective at 9:00 a.m. on gas day Monday, February 9, 2026. This posting complies with GT&C Section 23.6(h) of Natural's Tariff to describe the specific operational factors which caused the Operational Flow Order to be issued and to be lifted. ..

fields.body:
ANR/NGPL SOUTH JOLIET AT CAPACITY

SEGMENT
25 – STATION MAINTENANCE – CS 302

 

As
posted on Natural's Outage Impact Report (X25-1527903), Natural will be
performing station maintenance at Compressor Station 302 (CS 302) located in Montgomery
County, Texas (Segment 25 of Natural's Texok Zone).  Natural is required to
reduce the maximum operating capacity eastbound into Segment 25 from Segment 26
and Segment 22, thus limiting Natural's throughput capacity eastbound through
CS 302 during this restriction.

 

The

scheduling constraint will be at CS 302
; therefore, any gas received
west of CS 302 for delivery east of CS 302 will be impacted for the duration of
the restriction.  The Pooling Point - Texok Zone (LOC 10560) is located west of
the constraint.  Firm transportation associated with storage withdrawals may be
impacted.

 

As
such, effective for gas day 
Wednesday, April 1, 2026, Timely Cycle, and
continuing through gas day Friday, May 1, 2026
, Natural will schedule
Primary Firm and Secondary in-path Firm transports to no less than 
65%

of contract MDQ through CS 302.  AOR/ITS and Secondary out-of-path Firm
transports 
will not
 be available for the duration of this restriction.

 

The
stated scheduling percentage is based upon the current level of firm capacity
contracted for during this restriction and is subject to change based upon
operational conditions and Shipper utilization.

 

Continue
to monitor Natural's interactive website for any updates.  Please contact your

HOURLY TAKES ADVISORY – MARKET DELIVERY ZONE

HOURLY TAKES ADVISORY – MARKET
DELIVERY ZONE 

 

Due to the impending colder
weather and current system operating conditions, effective for
 Friday, December
 12, 2025, at 9:00 am., and continuing until further notice
, per Natural's
tariff [GT&C Section 7.4], 
Shippers and Point Operators
 are advised
to 
limit hourly
 
takes
 at 
ALL DELIVERY POINTS IN THE MARKET
DELIVERY ZONE
.  Additionally, Natural continues to monitor operating
conditions system wide.  If necessary, Natural will issue Operational Flow
Orders (OFOs) to address Shipper actions that are 
detrimental to such
operating conditions outside the Market Delivery Zone
.  Should Natural's
ability to provide hourly flexibility decrease, an Operational Flow Order (OFO)
condition will occur.

 

As provided in the tariff,
at each point in the Market Delivery Zone, the hourly rights for each Shipper/Point
Operator will be limited.  Such hourly rights will be limited by service
priority and nomination cycle, based on hours remaining in the gas day. 
Shippers and Point Operators are responsible for calculating and monitoring
their hourly usage so as not to exceed the limits described herein.

 

Hourly Rights for Firm
Service – 150%

Includes Primary and
Secondary Confirmed Nominations and Unused No-Notice firm service rights

 

            
Timely/Evening
Cycles

Limited to 
6.25% (150% / 24 hours)
 of Firm
Service.  

 

Intra-Day 1 Cycle

Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous
cycle for Firm Service; plus 
7.895%
 
(150% / 19 hours)
 of the difference
of current cycle Firm Service minus prior cycle Firm Service.  

 

Intra-Day 2 Cycle

Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous
cycle for Firm Service; plus
 10.00% (150% / 15 hours)
 of the difference
of current cycle Firm Service minus prior cycle Firm Service.  

 

Intra-Day 3 Cycle

Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous
cycle for Firm Service, plus 
13.64% (150% / 11 hours)
 of the difference
of current cycle Firm Service minus prior cycle Firm Service.

 

 

Hourly Rights for
Interruptible Service – 105%

Includes Interruptible and
AOR nominations, as well as POA tolerances

 

Timely/Evening
Cycles

Limited to 
4.375% (105% / 24 hours)
 of Interruptible
Service.  

 

Intra-Day 1 Cycle

Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous
cycle for Interruptible Service; plus
 5.53%
 
(105% / 19 hours)
 of
the difference of current cycle Interruptible Service minus prior cycle Interruptible
Service.  

 

 

Intra-Day 2 Cycle

Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous
cycle for Interruptible Service; plus 
7.0% (105% / 15 hours)
 of the
difference of current cycle Interruptible Service minus prior cycle Interruptible
Service.  

 

Intra-Day 3 Cycle

Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous
cycle for Interruptible Service; plus 
9.55% (105% / 11 hours)
 of the
difference of current cycle Interruptible Service minus prior cycle
Interruptible Service.

 

Limitation on
Nominations in All Cycles for Firm and Interruptible Service

 

Shippers are advised that nominations should be
received by Timely/Evening Cycle in order to utilize full rights over 24 hours,
to avoid exceeding the 24 hour ratable hourly takes calculation.  In all
cases, any first time nominations received on Non-Timely Cycles for full MDQ
utilization rights, plus any scheduled ITS nominations must conform to the 24
hour ratable calculation.  Shipper's hourly rights based on firm MDQ, plus
interruptible nominations, must be adequate enough to accommodate the
calculated hourly rights for the remaining hours of the gas day. 
Specifically, hourly rights cannot exceed 150% / 24 hours of Shipper's MDQ on
the nominated contract, plus 105% / 24 hours of Shipper's interruptible
nominations.

 

In addition, Natural would
like to remind point operators to utilize the Operator Point Reports available
on our website to assist you in monitoring your hourly takes.  These reports
are available by linking to http://pipeline.kindermorgan.com.  Select NGPL >
Customer Activities > Log On > Flowing Gas > Additional Reports >
NGPL/HRZ > NGPL/HRZ – Hourly Nomination Details.

 

Please contact your Account
Director or Scheduling Representative if you have any questions.

..

HOURLY TAKES ADVISORY – MARKET DELIVERY ZONE HOURLY TAKES ADVISORY – MARKET DELIVERY ZONE Due to the impending colder weather and current system operating conditions, effective for Friday, December 12, 2025, at 9:00 am., and continuing until further notice , per Natural's tariff [GT&C Section 7.4], Shippers and Point Operators are advised to limit hourly takes at ALL DELIVERY POINTS IN THE MARKET DELIVERY ZONE . Additionally, Natural continues to monitor operating conditions system wide. If necessary, Natural will issue Operational Flow Orders (OFOs) to address Shipper actions that are detrimental to such operating conditions outside the Market Delivery Zone . Should Natural's ability to provide hourly flexibility decrease, an Operational Flow Order (OFO) condition will occur. As provided in the tariff, at each point in the Market Delivery Zone, the hourly rights for each Shipper/Point Operator will be limited. Such hourly rights will be limited by service priority and nomination cycle, based on hours remaining in the gas day. Shippers and Point Operators are responsible for calculating and monitoring their hourly usage so as not to exceed the limits described herein. Hourly Rights for Firm Service – 150% Includes Primary and Secondary Confirmed Nominations and Unused No-Notice firm service rights Timely/Evening Cycles Limited to 6.25% (150% / 24 hours) of Firm Service. Intra-Day 1 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Firm Service; plus 7.895% (150% / 19 hours) of the difference of current cycle Firm Service minus prior cycle Firm Service. Intra-Day 2 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Firm Service; plus 10.00% (150% / 15 hours) of the difference of current cycle Firm Service minus prior cycle Firm Service. Intra-Day 3 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Firm Service, plus 13.64% (150% / 11 hours) of the difference of current cycle Firm Service minus prior cycle Firm Service. Hourly Rights for Interruptible Service – 105% Includes Interruptible and AOR nominations, as well as POA tolerances Timely/Evening Cycles Limited to 4.375% (105% / 24 hours) of Interruptible Service. Intra-Day 1 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Interruptible Service; plus 5.53% (105% / 19 hours) of the difference of current cycle Interruptible Service minus prior cycle Interruptible Service. Intra-Day 2 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Interruptible Service; plus 7.0% (105% / 15 hours) of the difference of current cycle Interruptible Service minus prior cycle Interruptible Service. Intra-Day 3 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Interruptible Service; plus 9.55% (105% / 11 hours) of the difference of current cycle Interruptible Service minus prior cycle Interruptible Service. Limitation on Nominations in All Cycles for Firm and Interruptible Service Shippers are advised that nominations should be received by Timely/Evening Cycle in order to utilize full rights over 24 hours, to avoid exceeding the 24 hour ratable hourly takes calculation. In all cases, any first time nominations received on Non-Timely Cycles for full MDQ utilization rights, plus any scheduled ITS nominations must conform to the 24 hour ratable calculation. Shipper's hourly rights based on firm MDQ, plus interruptible nominations, must be adequate enough to accommodate the calculated hourly rights for the remaining hours of the gas day. Specifically, hourly rights cannot exceed 150% / 24 hours of Shipper's MDQ on the nominated contract, plus 105% / 24 hours of Shipper's interruptible nominations. In addition, Natural would like to remind point operators to utilize the Operator Point Reports available on our website to assist you in monitoring your hourly takes. These reports are available by linking to http://pipeline.kindermorgan.com. Select NGPL > Customer Activities > Log On > Flowing Gas > Additional Reports > NGPL/HRZ > NGPL/HRZ – Hourly Nomination Details. Please contact your Account Director or Scheduling Representative if you have any questions. ..

HOURLY TAKES ADVISORY – MARKET DELIVERY ZONE HOURLY TAKES ADVISORY – MARKET DELIVERY ZONE Due to the impending colder weather and current system operating conditions, effective for Friday, December 12, 2025, at 9:00 am., and continuing until further notice , per Natural's tariff [GT&C Section 7.4], Shippers and Point Operators are advised to limit hourly takes at ALL DELIVERY POINTS IN THE MARKET DELIVERY ZONE . Additionally, Natural continues to monitor operating conditions system wide. If necessary, Natural will issue Operational Flow Orders (OFOs) to address Shipper actions that are detrimental to such operating conditions outside the Market Delivery Zone . Should Natural's ability to provide hourly flexibility decrease, an Operational Flow Order (OFO) condition will occur. As provided in the tariff, at each point in the Market Delivery Zone, the hourly rights for each Shipper/Point Operator will be limited. Such hourly rights will be limited by service priority and nomination cycle, based on hours remaining in the gas day. Shippers and Point Operators are responsible for calculating and monitoring their hourly usage so as not to exceed the limits described herein. Hourly Rights for Firm Service – 150% Includes Primary and Secondary Confirmed Nominations and Unused No-Notice firm service rights Timely/Evening Cycles Limited to 6.25% (150% / 24 hours) of Firm Service. Intra-Day 1 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Firm Service; plus 7.895% (150% / 19 hours) of the difference of current cycle Firm Service minus prior cycle Firm Service. Intra-Day 2 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Firm Service; plus 10.00% (150% / 15 hours) of the difference of current cycle Firm Service minus prior cycle Firm Service. Intra-Day 3 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Firm Service, plus 13.64% (150% / 11 hours) of the difference of current cycle Firm Service minus prior cycle Firm Service. Hourly Rights for Interruptible Service – 105% Includes Interruptible and AOR nominations, as well as POA tolerances Timely/Evening Cycles Limited to 4.375% (105% / 24 hours) of Interruptible Service. Intra-Day 1 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Interruptible Service; plus 5.53% (105% / 19 hours) of the difference of current cycle Interruptible Service minus prior cycle Interruptible Service. Intra-Day 2 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Interruptible Service; plus 7.0% (105% / 15 hours) of the difference of current cycle Interruptible Service minus prior cycle Interruptible Service. Intra-Day 3 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Interruptible Service; plus 9.55% (105% / 11 hours) of the difference of current cycle Interruptible Service minus prior cycle Interruptible Service. Limitation on Nominations in All Cycles for Firm and Interruptible Service Shippers are advised that nominations should be received by Timely/Evening Cycle in order to utilize full rights over 24 hours, to avoid exceeding the 24 hour ratable hourly takes calculation. In all cases, any first time nominations received on Non-Timely Cycles for full MDQ utilization rights, plus any scheduled ITS nominations must conform to the 24 hour ratable calculation. Shipper's hourly rights based on firm MDQ, plus interruptible nominations, must be adequate enough to accommodate the calculated hourly rights for the remaining hours of the gas day. Specifically, hourly rights cannot exceed 150% / 24 hours of Shipper's MDQ on the nominated contract, plus 105% / 24 hours of Shipper's interruptible nominations. In addition, Natural would like to remind point operators to utilize the Operator Point Reports available on our website to assist you in monitoring your hourly takes. These reports are available by linking to http://pipeline.kindermorgan.com. Select NGPL > Customer Activities > Log On > Flowing Gas > Additional Reports > NGPL/HRZ > NGPL/HRZ – Hourly Nomination Details. Please contact your Account Director or Scheduling Representative if you have any questions. ..

ANR/NGPL SOUTH JOLIET AT CAPACITY SEGMENT 25 – STATION MAINTENANCE – CS 302 As posted on Natural's Outage Impact Report (X25-1527903), Natural will be performing station maintenance at Compressor Station 302 (CS 302) located in Montgomery County, Texas (Segment 25 of Natural's Texok Zone). Natural is required to reduce the maximum operating capacity eastbound into Segment 25 from Segment 26 and Segment 22, thus limiting Natural's throughput capacity eastbound through CS 302 during this restriction. The scheduling constraint will be at CS 302 ; therefore, any gas received west of CS 302 for delivery east of CS 302 will be impacted for the duration of the restriction. The Pooling Point - Texok Zone (LOC 10560) is located west of the constraint. Firm transportation associated with storage withdrawals may be impacted. As such, effective for gas day Wednesday, April 1, 2026, Timely Cycle, and continuing through gas day Friday, May 1, 2026 , Natural will schedule Primary Firm and Secondary in-path Firm transports to no less than 55% of contract MDQ through CS 302. AOR/ITS and Secondary out-of-path Firm transports will not be available for the duration of this restriction. The stated scheduling percentage is based upon the current level of firm capacity contracted for during this restriction and is subject to change based upon operational conditions and Shipper utilization. Continue to monitor Natural's interactive website for any updates. Please contact your Account Director or Scheduling Representative if you have any questions. ..

OPERATIONAL
FLOW ORDER – MARKET DELIVERY ZONE – REPORT

On January 20, 2026, due
to forecasted colder than normal weather, expected increased load on its
system, anticipated maximum peaking withdrawals from storage facilities, and
system operating conditions, Natural issued an Operational Flow Order (“OFO”) in
the Market Delivery Zone effective for Thursday, January 22, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. Central
Clock Time. This action was taken in accordance with Section 23.6 of the
General Terms and Conditions of Natural's FERC Gas Tariff (“GT&C”).

The OFO was issued to
maintain and preserve the operational integrity of Natural's system and was in
response to the following operational factors: (1) to maintain pressures for
firm transportation deliveries in the Market Delivery Zone; and (2) maintain deliverability
from Natural's market area storage fields for firm storage services.

The OFO did not result in
any curtailment of primary firm service.  During the OFO, Natural implemented
daily and hourly take limitations for firm and interruptible Shippers
(including Point Operators) at all points in the Market Delivery Zone.  The OFO
limited Shippers and Point Operators, on a daily basis, from taking volumes in
excess of confirmed transportation nominations plus no-notice rights at
delivery points in the Market Delivery Zone, and on an hourly basis to 130% of
their firm service rights.  Hourly rights for interruptible nominations were
limited to 105% of the Shipper's interruptible nominations. Additionally,
Shippers and Point Operators were required to flow more ratably during the gas
day based on service priority and nomination cycles.  
The
firm service percentage was reduced to 110% on Tuesday, January 27, 2026 at
9:00 a.m. Central Clock Time, and then  increased back to 130% on Thursday
February 5, 2026 at 9:00 am Central Clock Time. 
 

These measures were taken
consistent with Natural's Tariff due to sustained colder than normal weather in
the Market Delivery Zone and anticipated maximum peaking withdrawals from
storage facilities.  As the weather conditions moderated and the associated
high gas demand declined, Natural removed the OFO, effective at 9:00 a.m. on
gas day Monday, February 9, 2026.

This posting complies
with GT&C Section 23.6(h) of Natural's Tariff to describe the specific
operational factors which caused the Operational Flow Order to be issued and to
be lifted.

PHMSA MEGA RULE–- ELIGIBLE
PROJECT
 - SEGMENT 13 – AMARILLO #3 M/L – CS 107/108 – ILI TOOL
RUNS

 

In accordance with its FERC
Gas Tariff and as posted on Natural's Outage Impact Report 
(X25-1166550)
; 
as part of
Natural's ongoing pipeline Integrity Management Program, Natural will perform a
series of ILI tool runs on its Amarillo #3 mainline between Compressor Station 107
(CS 107) located in Mills County, Iowa and Compressor Station 108 (CS 108)
located in Warren County, Iowa (Segment 13 of Natural's Amarillo Mainline Zone). 
The tool runs will require Natural to reduce the operating capacity, thus limiting
Natural's throughput capacity northbound through CS 108.  Once the data
from the tool runs have been analyzed, any remediation work impacting shippers
will be posted.

 

This remediation project is
pursuant to the PHMSA Mega Rule and as set forth in its Tariff, is an Eligible
Project (ID 4819) included on the Eligible Project List posted on Natural's
internet website.  See Eligible Project ID, line name and location
identified below (Appendix F- Docket No. RP22-1222 Settlement).  This
outage is subject to the provisions of Section 5.2 (c) (5) of the General
Terms and Conditions of Natural's FERC Gas Tariff.

 

Project
ID          Line
Name                  
              Location/Segment
No.                      
           

4819                  AMARILLO
#3 MAINLINE     SEGMENT 13

 

The scheduling
constraint will be upstream of CS 108 at the beginning of Segment 13;
therefore, any gas received south of Segment 13 for delivery north of Segment
13 will be impacted for the duration of the restriction.  Receipts from
Trailblazer Gage (LOC 902900) are south of CS 107 and will be impacted for the
duration of the restriction.  Northern Natural Mills (LOC 900203) is located
downstream of the Segment 13 constraint location.  For scheduling purposes, the
Amarillo Pool (LOC 10566) is located south of the constraint. 
Additionally, firm transportation associated with storage withdrawals or
injections may be impacted.

 

As such,
effective on the gas days indicated below, Natural will schedule Primary Firm and
Secondary in-path Firm transports to no less than 
44%
 of contract
MDQ northbound through CS 107.  AOR/ITS and Secondary out-of-path Firm
transports 
will not
 be available for the duration of the restriction.

DATES
:

April 17, 2026 (Cleaning/ Gauge Tools)

Gas day

April 23, 2026 (Cleaning Tool)

April 28, 2026 (Combo Tool)

Gas day Thursday,
April 30, 2026 (EMAT Tool)

Gas day

scheduling percentage is based upon the current level of firm capacity
contracted for during this restriction and is subject to change based upon
operational conditions and Shipper utilization.

 

Continue to
monitor Natural's interactive website for any updates to the end date and/or
scheduling percentage during this restriction.  Please contact your
Account Director or Scheduling Representative if you have any questions.

HOURLY TAKES ADVISORY – MARKET DELIVERY ZONE HOURLY TAKES ADVISORY – MARKET DELIVERY ZONE Due to the impending colder weather and current system operating conditions, effective for Friday, December 12, 2025, at 9:00 am., and continuing until further notice , per Natural's tariff [GT&C Section 7.4], Shippers and Point Operators are advised to limit hourly takes at ALL DELIVERY POINTS IN THE MARKET DELIVERY ZONE . Additionally, Natural continues to monitor operating conditions system wide. If necessary, Natural will issue Operational Flow Orders (OFOs) to address Shipper actions that are detrimental to such operating conditions outside the Market Delivery Zone . Should Natural's ability to provide hourly flexibility decrease, an Operational Flow Order (OFO) condition will occur. As provided in the tariff, at each point in the Market Delivery Zone, the hourly rights for each Shipper/Point Operator will be limited. Such hourly rights will be limited by service priority and nomination cycle, based on hours remaining in the gas day. Shippers and Point Operators are responsible for calculating and monitoring their hourly usage so as not to exceed the limits described herein. Hourly Rights for Firm Service – 150% Includes Primary and Secondary Confirmed Nominations and Unused No-Notice firm service rights Timely/Evening Cycles Limited to 6.25% (150% / 24 hours) of Firm Service. Intra-Day 1 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Firm Service; plus 7.895% (150% / 19 hours) of the difference of current cycle Firm Service minus prior cycle Firm Service. Intra-Day 2 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Firm Service; plus 10.00% (150% / 15 hours) of the difference of current cycle Firm Service minus prior cycle Firm Service. Intra-Day 3 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Firm Service, plus 13.64% (150% / 11 hours) of the difference of current cycle Firm Service minus prior cycle Firm Service. Hourly Rights for Interruptible Service – 105% Includes Interruptible and AOR nominations, as well as POA tolerances Timely/Evening Cycles Limited to 4.375% (105% / 24 hours) of Interruptible Service. Intra-Day 1 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Interruptible Service; plus 5.53% (105% / 19 hours) of the difference of current cycle Interruptible Service minus prior cycle Interruptible Service. Intra-Day 2 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Interruptible Service; plus 7.0% (105% / 15 hours) of the difference of current cycle Interruptible Service minus prior cycle Interruptible Service. Intra-Day 3 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Interruptible Service; plus 9.55% (105% / 11 hours) of the difference of current cycle Interruptible Service minus prior cycle Interruptible Service. Limitation on Nominations in All Cycles for Firm and Interruptible Service Shippers are advised that nominations should be received by Timely/Evening Cycle in order to utilize full rights over 24 hours, to avoid exceeding the 24 hour ratable hourly takes calculation. In all cases, any first time nominations received on Non-Timely Cycles for full MDQ utilization rights, plus any scheduled ITS nominations must conform to the 24 hour ratable calculation. Shipper's hourly rights based on firm MDQ, plus interruptible nominations, must be adequate enough to accommodate the calculated hourly rights for the remaining hours of the gas day. Specifically, hourly rights cannot exceed 150% / 24 hours of Shipper's MDQ on the nominated contract, plus 105% / 24 hours of Shipper's interruptible nominations. In addition, Natural would like to remind point operators to utilize the Operator Point Reports available on our website to assist you in monitoring your hourly takes. These reports are available by linking to http://pipeline.kindermorgan.com. Select NGPL > Customer Activities > Log On > Flowing Gas > Additional Reports > NGPL/HRZ > NGPL/HRZ – Hourly Nomination Details. Please contact your Account Director or Scheduling Representative if you have any questions. ..

OPERATIONAL FLOW ORDER – MARKET DELIVERY ZONE – REPORT On January 20, 2026, due to forecasted colder than normal weather, expected increased load on its system, anticipated maximum peaking withdrawals from storage facilities, and system operating conditions, Natural issued an Operational Flow Order (“OFO”) in the Market Delivery Zone effective for Thursday, January 22, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. Central Clock Time. This action was taken in accordance with Section 23.6 of the General Terms and Conditions of Natural's FERC Gas Tariff (“GT&C”). The OFO was issued to maintain and preserve the operational integrity of Natural's system and was in response to the following operational factors: (1) to maintain pressures for firm transportation deliveries in the Market Delivery Zone; and (2) maintain deliverability from Natural's market area storage fields for firm storage services. The OFO did not result in any curtailment of primary firm service. During the OFO, Natural implemented daily and hourly take limitations for firm and interruptible Shippers (including Point Operators) at all points in the Market Delivery Zone. The OFO limited Shippers and Point Operators, on a daily basis, from taking volumes in excess of confirmed transportation nominations plus no-notice rights at delivery points in the Market Delivery Zone, and on an hourly basis to 130% of their firm service rights. Hourly rights for interruptible nominations were limited to 105% of the Shipper's interruptible nominations. Additionally, Shippers and Point Operators were required to flow more ratably during the gas day based on service priority and nomination cycles. The firm service percentage was reduced to 110% on Tuesday, January 27, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. Central Clock Time, and then increased back to 130% on Thursday February 5, 2026 at 9:00 am Central Clock Time. These measures were taken consistent with Natural's Tariff due to sustained colder than normal weather in the Market Delivery Zone and anticipated maximum peaking withdrawals from storage facilities. As the weather conditions moderated and the associated high gas demand declined, Natural removed the OFO, effective at 9:00 a.m. on gas day Monday, February 9, 2026. This posting complies with GT&C Section 23.6(h) of Natural's Tariff to describe the specific operational factors which caused the Operational Flow Order to be issued and to be lifted. ..

HOURLY TAKES ADVISORY – MARKET DELIVERY ZONE HOURLY TAKES ADVISORY – MARKET DELIVERY ZONE Due to the impending colder weather and current system operating conditions, effective for Friday, December 12, 2025, at 9:00 am., and continuing until further notice , per Natural's tariff [GT&C Section 7.4], Shippers and Point Operators are advised to limit hourly takes at ALL DELIVERY POINTS IN THE MARKET DELIVERY ZONE . Additionally, Natural continues to monitor operating conditions system wide. If necessary, Natural will issue Operational Flow Orders (OFOs) to address Shipper actions that are detrimental to such operating conditions outside the Market Delivery Zone . Should Natural's ability to provide hourly flexibility decrease, an Operational Flow Order (OFO) condition will occur. As provided in the tariff, at each point in the Market Delivery Zone, the hourly rights for each Shipper/Point Operator will be limited. Such hourly rights will be limited by service priority and nomination cycle, based on hours remaining in the gas day. Shippers and Point Operators are responsible for calculating and monitoring their hourly usage so as not to exceed the limits described herein. Hourly Rights for Firm Service – 150% Includes Primary and Secondary Confirmed Nominations and Unused No-Notice firm service rights Timely/Evening Cycles Limited to 6.25% (150% / 24 hours) of Firm Service. Intra-Day 1 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Firm Service; plus 7.895% (150% / 19 hours) of the difference of current cycle Firm Service minus prior cycle Firm Service. Intra-Day 2 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Firm Service; plus 10.00% (150% / 15 hours) of the difference of current cycle Firm Service minus prior cycle Firm Service. Intra-Day 3 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Firm Service, plus 13.64% (150% / 11 hours) of the difference of current cycle Firm Service minus prior cycle Firm Service. Hourly Rights for Interruptible Service – 105% Includes Interruptible and AOR nominations, as well as POA tolerances Timely/Evening Cycles Limited to 4.375% (105% / 24 hours) of Interruptible Service. Intra-Day 1 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Interruptible Service; plus 5.53% (105% / 19 hours) of the difference of current cycle Interruptible Service minus prior cycle Interruptible Service. Intra-Day 2 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Interruptible Service; plus 7.0% (105% / 15 hours) of the difference of current cycle Interruptible Service minus prior cycle Interruptible Service. Intra-Day 3 Cycle Limited to the hourly rights computed in the previous cycle for Interruptible Service; plus 9.55% (105% / 11 hours) of the difference of current cycle Interruptible Service minus prior cycle Interruptible Service. Limitation on Nominations in All Cycles for Firm and Interruptible Service Shippers are advised that nominations should be received by Timely/Evening Cycle in order to utilize full rights over 24 hours, to avoid exceeding the 24 hour ratable hourly takes calculation. In all cases, any first time nominations received on Non-Timely Cycles for full MDQ utilization rights, plus any scheduled ITS nominations must conform to the 24 hour ratable calculation. Shipper's hourly rights based on firm MDQ, plus interruptible nominations, must be adequate enough to accommodate the calculated hourly rights for the remaining hours of the gas day. Specifically, hourly rights cannot exceed 150% / 24 hours of Shipper's MDQ on the nominated contract, plus 105% / 24 hours of Shipper's interruptible nominations. In addition, Natural would like to remind point operators to utilize the Operator Point Reports available on our website to assist you in monitoring your hourly takes. These reports are available by linking to http://pipeline.kindermorgan.com. Select NGPL > Customer Activities > Log On > Flowing Gas > Additional Reports > NGPL/HRZ > NGPL/HRZ – Hourly Nomination Details. Please contact your Account Director or Scheduling Representative if you have any questions. ..

OPERATIONAL FLOW ORDER – MARKET DELIVERY ZONE – REPORT On January 20, 2026, due to forecasted colder than normal weather, expected increased load on its system, anticipated maximum peaking withdrawals from storage facilities, and system operating conditions, Natural issued an Operational Flow Order (“OFO”) in the Market Delivery Zone effective for Thursday, January 22, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. Central Clock Time. This action was taken in accordance with Section 23.6 of the General Terms and Conditions of Natural's FERC Gas Tariff (“GT&C”). The OFO was issued to maintain and preserve the operational integrity of Natural's system and was in response to the following operational factors: (1) to maintain pressures for firm transportation deliveries in the Market Delivery Zone; and (2) maintain deliverability from Natural's market area storage fields for firm storage services. The OFO did not result in any curtailment of primary firm service. During the OFO, Natural implemented daily and hourly take limitations for firm and interruptible Shippers (including Point Operators) at all points in the Market Delivery Zone. The OFO limited Shippers and Point Operators, on a daily basis, from taking volumes in excess of confirmed transportation nominations plus no-notice rights at delivery points in the Market Delivery Zone, and on an hourly basis to 130% of their firm service rights. Hourly rights for interruptible nominations were limited to 105% of the Shipper's interruptible nominations. Additionally, Shippers and Point Operators were required to flow more ratably during the gas day based on service priority and nomination cycles. The firm service percentage was reduced to 110% on Tuesday, January 27, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. Central Clock Time, and then increased back to 130% on Thursday February 5, 2026 at 9:00 am Central Clock Time. These measures were taken consistent with Natural's Tariff due to sustained colder than normal weather in the Market Delivery Zone and anticipated maximum peaking withdrawals from storage facilities. As the weather conditions moderated and the associated high gas demand declined, Natural removed the OFO, effective at 9:00 a.m. on gas day Monday, February 9, 2026. This posting complies with GT&C Section 23.6(h) of Natural's Tariff to describe the specific operational factors which caused the Operational Flow Order to be issued and to be lifted. ..
